arguments.explanation: Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was newly started on 2026-03-02 at a cardiology clinic visit. Because the start is on or after 2026-03-01, the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07, five days after the start, showing sinus rhythm with QTc 381 ms, so the requirement was met.

items.explanation: 80-year-old woman (DOB 1945-10-26) whose cardiology clinic notes from 2025-09-12 through 2026-06-22 all carry a problem list of persistent atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: congestive heart failure (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure / acute on chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure) 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes mellitus 1, prior stroke/TIA 2 (personal history of TIA and cerebral infarction, hemiplegia and dysarthria following cerebral infarction) 2, vascular disease (old myocardial infarction, coronary atherosclerosis) 1, female sex 1. No anticoagulant is active as of 2026-09-24: the only current orders are aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin, and every clinic note lists no anticoagulant. Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent and aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis for AF.

Patient is on continuous escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current order authored 2026-07-18, valid to 2026-12-26; therapy has run without interruption since May 2024). The most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 500 ms at RR 880 ms, QTc (Bazett) 533 ms - above the 500 ms threshold requiring prescriber review. The preceding ECG of 2022-11-23 had a QTc of 355 ms, so this represents a marked increase. Note the clinic note of 2024-05-14 reviewed this same tracing as 'sinus rhythm, QT acceptable' before starting escitalopram, which the measured QTc does not support. Most recent electrolytes: potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-03-18), both at the low end of normal and worth optimising.

Patient is taking citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current order authored 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-07; continuous therapy since 2023). The most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70/min with QT 506 ms at RR 856 ms, QTc (Bazett) 547 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold; the earlier ECG of 2020-06-17 had a QTc of 445 ms. Most recent electrolytes are potassium 4.6 mEq/L (2026-07-15) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08). The dose of 40 mg daily also exceeds the 20 mg maximum recommended in patients at risk of QT prolongation, so both dose and continued use require prescriber review, with a repeat ECG.

Amiodarone (QT watch-list) was started on 2025-11-10 at a cardiology clinic visit, after the 2025-09-01 memo took effect and before the 2026-03-01 revision, so the required window is an ECG within 30 days, i.e. by 2025-12-10. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was met. (The ECG itself showed QTc 556 ms - flagged separately as a QT safety item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was newly started on 2026-02-12 at a cardiology clinic visit. Because the start date precedes 2026-03-01, the 2025-09-01 memo applies and an ECG was required within 30 days, i.e. by 2026-03-14. ECG 101538691 was obtained on 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was met. That ECG showed sinus rhythm with QTc 484 ms, prolonged but below the 500 ms prescriber-review threshold.

71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 encounter and carried in every subsequent cardiology clinic note (2025-10-10 to 2026-06-27). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease 1 (coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery with prior bypass/graft surgery). A score of >=2 in a man warrants oral anticoagulation, but no anticoagulant order is active on 2026-09-24 (current medication is levothyroxine only; amiodarone in August 2025 was a short inpatient course). He also has a coded history of haemorrhage complicating a procedure, so the bleeding/benefit balance should be documented when anticoagulation is discussed.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: prior ischaemic stroke 2 (cerebral infarction due to embolism, hemiplegia/hemiparesis and facial weakness following cerebral infarction), hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female sex 1. Anticoagulation is strongly recommended for AF with a prior embolic stroke, yet no anticoagulant is current on 2026-09-24 - her active medications are famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol only, and all clinic notes from 2025-04-24 to 2026-06-23 say 'continue current regimen'. Documented thrombocytopenia and a history of falling should be weighed but do not by themselves remove the indication.

48-year-old man (DOB 1978-02-27) whose cardiology clinic notes from 2025-07-19 to 2026-08-04 list paroxysmal atrial fibrillation as an active problem. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2: heart failure 1 (congestive heart failure, acute systolic heart failure and other primary cardiomyopathy coded at the 2025-02-26 admission, with a personal history of sudden cardiac arrest) and hypertension 1. A CHA2DS2-VASc of 2 in a man corresponds to an annual thromboembolic risk of about 2% and anticoagulation is recommended. He has a 'long-term current use of anticoagulants' code from 2025-06-17 but no anticoagulant order is active on 2026-09-24 (current medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline), so his anticoagulation status needs to be clarified.

Resumption, timing, the need for continued aspirin/clopidogrel, and gastroprotection all require prescriber review.

Concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban gives no added benefit and substantially increases bleeding risk (he also has current clopidogrel, prior rectal haemorrhage, thrombocytopenia and anaemia); one agent must be discontinued.

The note's rhythm statement is erroneous and should be corrected so the record reflects the diagnosis actually made.

71-year-old woman (DOB 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented at the 2025-03-14 encounter (the same-day ECG 102298909 shows sinus rhythm with an atrial ectopic, which is compatible with paroxysmal AF). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: prior ischaemic stroke 2 (cerebral infarction due to embolism, hemiplegia/hemiparesis and facial weakness following cerebral infarction), hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female sex 1. Anticoagulation is strongly recommended for AF with a prior embolic stroke, yet no anticoagulant is current on 2026-09-24 - her active medications are famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol only, and all clinic notes from 2025-04-24 to 2026-06-23 say 'continue current regimen'. Sinus rhythm at 66/min, PR 156 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 367 ms, QTc 385 ms. Axis -20 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart.

He also has a coded history of haemorrhage complicating a procedure, so the bleeding/benefit balance should be documented when anticoagulation is discussed.

A CHA2DS2-VASc of 2 in a man corresponds to an annual thromboembolic risk of about 2% and anticoagulation is recommended. He has a 'long-term current use of anticoagulants' code from 2025-06-17 but no anticoagulant order is active on 2026-09-24 (current medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline), so his anticoagulation status needs to be clarified.

items.explanation: 80-year-old woman (DOB 1945-10-26) whose cardiology clinic notes from 2025-09-12 through 2026-06-22 all carry a problem list of persistent atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: congestive heart failure (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure / acute on chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure) 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes mellitus 1, prior stroke/TIA 2 (personal history of TIA and cerebral infarction, hemiplegia and dysarthria following cerebral infarction) 2, vascular disease (old myocardial infarction, coronary atherosclerosis) 1, female sex 1. No anticoagulant is active as of 2026-09-24: the only current orders are aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin, and every clinic note lists no anticoagulant. Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent and aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis for AF.

Patient is on continuous escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current order authored 2026-07-18, valid to 2026-12-26; therapy has run without interruption since May 2024). The most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 500 ms at RR 880 ms, QTc (Bazett) 533 ms - above the 500 ms threshold requiring prescriber review. The preceding ECG of 2022-11-23 had a QTc of 355 ms, so this represents a marked increase. Note the clinic note of 2024-05-14 reviewed this same tracing as 'sinus rhythm, QT acceptable' before starting escitalopram, which the measured QTc does not support. Most recent electrolytes: potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-03-18), both at the low end of normal and worth optimising.

Patient is taking citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current order authored 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-07; continuous therapy since 2023). The dose of 40 mg daily also exceeds the 20 mg maximum recommended in patients at risk of QT prolongation, so both dose and continued use require prescriber review, with a repeat ECG.

ECG 104882441 was recorded on 2026-03-07, five days after the start, showing sinus rhythm with QTc 381 ms, so the requirement was met.

71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 encounter and carried in every subsequent cardiology clinic note (2025-10-10 to 2026-06-27). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease 1 (coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery with prior bypass/graft surgery). A score of >=2 in a man warrants oral anticoagulation, but no anticoagulant order is active on 2026-09-24 (current medication is levothyroxine only; amiodarone in August 2025 was a short inpatient course). He also has a coded history of haemorrhage complicating a procedure, so the bleeding/benefit balance should be documented when anticoagulation is discussed.

71-year-old woman (DOB 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented at the 2025-03-14 encounter (the same-day ECG 102298909 shows sinus rhythm with an atrial ectopic, which is compatible with paroxysmal AF). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: prior ischaemic stroke 2 (cerebral infarction due to embolism, hemiplegia/hemiparesis and facial weakness following cerebral infarction), hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female sex 1. Anticoagulation is strongly recommended for AF with a prior embolic stroke, yet no anticoagulant is current on 2026-09-24 - her active medications are famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol only, and all clinic notes from 2025-04-24 to 2026-06-23 say 'continue current regimen'. Documented thrombocytopenia and a history of falling should be weighed but do not by themselves remove the indication.

48-year-old man (DOB 1978-02-27) whose cardiology clinic notes from 2025-07-19 to 2026-08-04 list paroxysmal atrial fibrillation as an active problem. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2: heart failure 1 (congestive heart failure, acute systolic heart failure and other primary cardiomyopathy coded at the 2025-02-26 admission, with a personal history of sudden cardiac arrest) and hypertension 1. A CHA2DS2-VASc of 2 in a man corresponds to an annual thromboembolic risk of about 2% and anticoagulation is recommended. He has a 'long-term current use of anticoagulants' code from 2025-06-17 but no anticoagulant order is active on 2026-09-24 (current medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline), so his anticoagulation status needs to be clarified.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered on 2026-08-20 (valid to 2027-01-04) and is the current anticoagulant. Eight days earlier, the summary of episode note of 2026-08-12 recorded outside records from Mercy Hospital: admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper gastrointestinal bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, two units transfused, and 'apixaban held at discharge pending cardiology review'. The 2026-08-20 clinic note simply says 'no changes today' and lists apixaban, aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg as current - i.e. triple antithrombotic therapy was resumed after a transfusion-requiring GI bleed without any documented review of the decision. Resumption, timing, the need for continued aspirin/clopidogrel, and gastroprotection all require prescriber review.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active for this patient with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter: apixaban 5 mg tablet ordered 2026-07-15 (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg tablet ordered two minutes later the same day (valid 2026-07-15 to 2027-01-03). Both cover the evaluation time of 2026-09-24 12:00 and neither has been stopped. Concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban gives no added benefit and substantially increases bleeding risk (he also has current clopidogrel, prior rectal haemorrhage, thrombocytopenia and anaemia); one agent must be discontinued.

Consistent with the ECGs, unspecified atrial fibrillation was coded at the 2026-06-10 encounter and warfarin was started the same day. The note's rhythm statement is erroneous and should be corrected so the record reflects the diagnosis actually made.

No ECG has been recorded since 2022 despite years of amiodarone, so prescriber review and a current ECG are needed.

items.explanation: 80-year-old woman (DOB 1945-10-26) whose cardiology clinic notes from 2025-09-12 through 2026-06-22 all carry a problem list of persistent atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: congestive heart failure (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure / acute on chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure) 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes mellitus 1, prior stroke/TIA 2 (personal history of TIA and cerebral infarction, hemiplegia and dysarthria following cerebral infarction) 2, vascular disease (old myocardial infarction, coronary atherosclerosis) 1, female sex 1. No anticoagulant is active as of 2026-09-24: the only current orders are aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin, and every clinic note lists no anticoagulant. Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent and aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis for AF.

Patient is on continuous escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current order authored 2026-07-18, valid to 2026-12-26; therapy has run without interruption since May 2024). The most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 500 ms at RR 880 ms, QTc (Bazett) 533 ms - above the 500 ms threshold requiring prescriber review. The preceding ECG of 2022-11-23 had a QTc of 355 ms, so this represents a marked increase. Note the clinic note of 2024-05-14 reviewed this same tracing as 'sinus rhythm, QT acceptable' before starting escitalopram, which the measured QTc does not support. Most recent electrolytes: potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-03-18), both at the low end of normal and worth optimising.

Most recent electrolytes are potassium 4.6 mEq/L (2026-07-15) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08). The dose of 40 mg daily also exceeds the 20 mg maximum recommended in patients at risk of QT prolongation, so both dose and continued use require prescriber review, with a repeat ECG.

A score of >=2 in a man warrants oral anticoagulation, but no anticoagulant order is active on 2026-09-24 (current medication is levothyroxine only; amiodarone in August 2025 was a short inpatient course). He also has a coded history of haemorrhage complicating a procedure, so the bleeding/benefit balance should be documented when anticoagulation is discussed.

Anticoagulation is strongly recommended for AF with a prior embolic stroke, yet no anticoagulant is current on 2026-09-24 - her active medications are famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol only, and all clinic notes from 2025-04-24 to 2026-06-23 say 'continue current regimen'. Documented thrombocytopenia and a history of falling should be weighed but do not by themselves remove the indication.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 2: heart failure 1 (congestive heart failure, acute systolic heart failure and other primary cardiomyopathy coded at the 2025-02-26 admission, with a personal history of sudden cardiac arrest) and hypertension 1. A CHA2DS2-VASc of 2 in a man corresponds to an annual thromboembolic risk of about 2% and anticoagulation is recommended. He has a 'long-term current use of anticoagulants' code from 2025-06-17 but no anticoagulant order is active on 2026-09-24 (current medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline), so his anticoagulation status needs to be clarified.

Resumption, timing, the need for continued aspirin/clopidogrel, and gastroprotection all require prescriber review.

The note's rhythm statement is erroneous and should be corrected so the record reflects the diagnosis actually made.

arguments.explanation: Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started on 2026-09-15 at a cardiology clinic visit (the only previous exposure was a brief inpatient course in Feb-Mar 2025). Under the revised 2026-03-01 memo an ECG is required within 14 days of the start, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since the start (most recent tracing 104253928, 2025-03-09, QTc 415 ms), but the deadline falls after the evaluation date of 2026-09-24, so the requirement is not yet due; the ECG should be arranged before 2026-09-29.

items.explanation: 80-year-old woman (DOB 1945-10-26) whose cardiology clinic notes from 2025-09-12 through 2026-06-22 all carry a problem list of persistent atrial fibrillation. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9: congestive heart failure (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure / acute on chronic combined systolic and diastolic heart failure) 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, type 2 diabetes mellitus 1, prior stroke/TIA 2 (personal history of TIA and cerebral infarction, hemiplegia and dysarthria following cerebral infarction) 2, vascular disease (old myocardial infarction, coronary atherosclerosis) 1, female sex 1. No anticoagulant is active as of 2026-09-24: the only current orders are aspirin 81 mg daily and gabapentin, and every clinic note lists no anticoagulant. Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is absent and aspirin alone is not adequate stroke prophylaxis for AF.

Patient is on continuous escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current order authored 2026-07-18, valid to 2026-12-26; therapy has run without interruption since May 2024). The most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68/min with QT 500 ms at RR 880 ms, QTc (Bazett) 533 ms - above the 500 ms threshold requiring prescriber review. The preceding ECG of 2022-11-23 had a QTc of 355 ms, so this represents a marked increase. Note the clinic note of 2024-05-14 reviewed this same tracing as 'sinus rhythm, QT acceptable' before starting escitalopram, which the measured QTc does not support. Most recent electrolytes: potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-03-18), both at the low end of normal and worth optimising.

Patient is taking citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current order authored 2026-07-15, valid to 2027-01-07; continuous therapy since 2023). Most recent electrolytes are potassium 4.6 mEq/L (2026-07-15) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08). Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was newly started on 2026-02-12 at a cardiology clinic visit. 71-year-old man (DOB 1955-08-23) with atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 encounter and carried in every subsequent cardiology clinic note (2025-10-10 to 2026-06-27). CHA2DS2-VASc = 3: hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, vascular disease 1 (coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery with prior bypass/graft surgery). A score of >=2 in a man warrants oral anticoagulation, but no anticoagulant order is active on 2026-09-24 (current medication is levothyroxine only; amiodarone in August 2025 was a short inpatient course). He also has a coded history of haemorrhage complicating a procedure, so the bleeding/benefit balance should be documented when anticoagulation is discussed.

71-year-old woman (DOB 1955-09-07) with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented at the 2025-03-14 encounter (the same-day ECG 102298909 shows sinus rhythm with an atrial ectopic, which is compatible with paroxysmal AF). CHA2DS2-VASc = 5: prior ischaemic stroke 2 (cerebral infarction due to embolism, hemiplegia/hemiparesis and facial weakness following cerebral infarction), hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female sex 1. Anticoagulation is strongly recommended for AF with a prior embolic stroke, yet no anticoagulant is current on 2026-09-24 - her active medications are famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol only, and all clinic notes from 2025-04-24 to 2026-06-23 say 'continue current regimen'. Documented thrombocytopenia and a history of falling should be weighed but do not by themselves remove the indication.

48-year-old man (DOB 1978-02-27) whose cardiology clinic notes from 2025-07-19 to 2026-08-04 list paroxysmal atrial fibrillation as an active problem. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2: heart failure 1 (congestive heart failure, acute systolic heart failure and other primary cardiomyopathy coded at the 2025-02-26 admission, with a personal history of sudden cardiac arrest) and hypertension 1. A CHA2DS2-VASc of 2 in a man corresponds to an annual thromboembolic risk of about 2% and anticoagulation is recommended. He has a 'long-term current use of anticoagulants' code from 2025-06-17 but no anticoagulant order is active on 2026-09-24 (current medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline), so his anticoagulation status needs to be clarified.

Eight days earlier, the summary of episode note of 2026-08-12 recorded outside records from Mercy Hospital: admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper gastrointestinal bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, two units transfused, and 'apixaban held at discharge pending cardiology review'. Resumption, timing, the need for continued aspirin/clopidogrel, and gastroprotection all require prescriber review.

Both cover the evaluation time of 2026-09-24 12:00 and neither has been stopped. Concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban gives no added benefit and substantially increases bleeding risk (he also has current clopidogrel, prior rectal haemorrhage, thrombocytopenia and anaemia); one agent must be discontinued.

The note's rhythm statement is erroneous and should be corrected so the record reflects the diagnosis actually made.

Sinus rhythm at 74/min, PR 182 ms (upper normal), QRS 84 ms, QT 381 ms, QTc 423 ms. Axis +53 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min with one atrial premature beat (RR 538 ms) followed by a compensatory pause (1368 ms); the remaining RR intervals are regular at ~980 ms, so this is sinus rhythm with ectopy rather than atrial fibrillation (organised, reproducible P waves are present, PR 196 ms). Sinus rhythm at 70/min, regular, PR 142 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 355 ms, QTc 381 ms. Sinus rhythm at 68/min, PR 146 ms, QRS 80 ms. Axis +59 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Sinus bradycardia at 53/min, PR 172 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 385 ms, QTc 361 ms, axis -5 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Prior ECG 2018-12-13: sinus rhythm 66/min, PR 202 ms, QRS 102 ms, QTc 389 ms. Neither tracing shows a complete bundle branch block and the QTc change is only 28 ms, so no changes are flagged.

Sinus rhythm at 68/min, PR 128 ms, QRS 90 ms. Markedly prolonged repolarisation: QT 500 ms at RR 880 ms giving QTc (Bazett) 533 ms, with a broad late-peaking T wave maximal in V3. Axis +47 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Prior ECG 2022-11-23 had QTc 355 ms, so the QTc has increased by ~178 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60). Patient is on escitalopram - see QT safety review item.

Sinus tachycardia at 141/min: the rhythm is regular (RR 402-454 ms, CV 0.02) and a single low-amplitude but reproducible atrial wave (upright in II, III and aVF, inverted in aVR, ~0.06 mV) precedes each QRS with PR ~120-140 ms, followed by an isoelectric PR segment; there is one atrial complex per QRS, so this is not 2:1 flutter. Sinus rhythm at 82/min, PR 156 ms, QRS 100 ms (mild non-specific intraventricular conduction delay but not a complete bundle branch block), QT 378 ms, QTc 443 ms. Axis +33 degrees (normal). Only ECG in the chart.

Sinus rhythm at 91/min. The P wave is broad and notched (duration ~130 ms, left atrial abnormality) and the PR interval is 214 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 78 ms, QT 335 ms, QTc 412 ms, axis -17 degrees (normal). Prior ECG 2021-05-16: sinus rhythm 87/min, PR 144 ms, QRS 78 ms, QTc 391 ms. The PR interval has lengthened but there is no new bundle branch block, rhythm change or 60 ms QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 59/min with PR 214 ms (first-degree AV block). QRS is broad at 128 ms with a broad monophasic R wave in I, aVL and V6 (intrinsicoid deflection ~60-70 ms, no septal q) and a small r with a deep wide S in V1-V3 - complete left bundle branch block. QT 445 ms, QTc 449 ms. Axis -21 degrees (normal quadrant). The prior ECG of 2024-06-03 showed the same left bundle branch block with PR 212 ms, QRS 128 ms and QTc 457 ms, so there is no change.

Sinus rhythm at 102/min, PR 138 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 332 ms, QTc 432 ms, axis +46 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. The prior ECG from the previous day (2025-03-18: 101/min, PR 128 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc 428 ms) is essentially identical - no change.
Sinus rhythm at 66/min, PR 156 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 367 ms, QTc 385 ms. Axis -20 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart.

Sinus rhythm/sinus bradycardia at 58/min with organised upright P waves in II and a PR interval of about 200 ms (upper limit of normal, not counted as first-degree block). QRS 86 ms, axis +36 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged: QT 575 ms at RR 1042 ms, QTc (Bazett) 563 ms. The prior ECG of 2022-04-06 showed atrial fibrillation at ~130/min (RR CV 0.19, no P waves) with QTc 418 ms, so sinus rhythm has been restored (RESOLVED_AF) and the QTc has risen by ~145 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60). Patient remains on amiodarone - see QT safety review item.

Sinus tachycardia at 107/min, regular, PR 162 ms, QRS 66 ms, QT 318 ms, QTc 425 ms, axis +52 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Prior ECG 2019-07-27: sinus rhythm 75/min, PR 154 ms, QRS 68 ms, QTc 427 ms - no change other than the faster rate.

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular. Upright P in II with PR 126 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 301 ms, QTc 427 ms. Axis +67 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. This is the patient's only ECG, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102/min, PR 144 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 323 ms, QTc 420 ms, axis +58 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Compared with the ECG recorded 34 seconds earlier the same day (102910502: 100/min, PR 142 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 415 ms) the tracings are essentially identical - no change.

Sinus bradycardia at 52/min, regular. P waves upright in II (duration ~114 ms, suggesting left atrial abnormality) with PR 170 ms. QRS 90 ms, QT 432 ms, QTc 401 ms. Axis +36 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Prior ECG 2023-05-22 showed sinus rhythm ~58/min with a single atrial ectopic beat, PR 152 ms, QTc 391 ms - no significant change.

Sinus tachycardia at 122/min, perfectly regular (RR 492-496 ms). P upright in I/II with PR 126 ms. QRS is now narrow at 88 ms with generalised low voltage and an RS pattern in most leads; net QRS forces are rightward/inferior giving a frontal axis of roughly +110 to +140 degrees (right axis deviation). QT 294 ms, QTc 418 ms. Compared with the ECG from earlier the same day (106516875, 01:33: sinus 100/min with complete RBBB, QRS 150 ms, rSR' in V1 and broad terminal S in I/V6, QTc 472 ms) the right bundle branch block has resolved (RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK); the QTc fell by 54 ms, which does not reach the 60 ms threshold.

Sinus rhythm at 62/min, PR 172 ms, QRS 96 ms (no bundle branch block), axis +66 degrees (normal). Prior ECG 2025-06-07 had QTc 411 ms, an increase of ~145 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60), coinciding with amiodarone started 2025-11-10. See QT safety review item.

Documented thrombocytopenia and a history of falling should be weighed but do not by themselves remove the indication.

48-year-old man (DOB 1978-02-27) whose cardiology clinic notes from 2025-07-19 to 2026-08-04 list paroxysmal atrial fibrillation as an active problem. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2: heart failure 1 (congestive heart failure, acute systolic heart failure and other primary cardiomyopathy coded at the 2025-02-26 admission, with a personal history of sudden cardiac arrest) and hypertension 1. A CHA2DS2-VASc of 2 in a man corresponds to an annual thromboembolic risk of about 2% and anticoagulation is recommended. He has a 'long-term current use of anticoagulants' code from 2025-06-17 but no anticoagulant order is active on 2026-09-24 (current medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline), so his anticoagulation status needs to be clarified.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered on 2026-08-20 (valid to 2027-01-04) and is the current anticoagulant. Eight days earlier, the summary of episode note of 2026-08-12 recorded outside records from Mercy Hospital: admission 2026-08-02 to 2026-08-05 for upper gastrointestinal bleeding from a duodenal ulcer, haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, two units transfused, and 'apixaban held at discharge pending cardiology review'. The 2026-08-20 clinic note simply says 'no changes today' and lists apixaban, aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg as current - i.e. triple antithrombotic therapy was resumed after a transfusion-requiring GI bleed without any documented review of the decision. Resumption, timing, the need for continued aspirin/clopidogrel, and gastroprotection all require prescriber review.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active for this patient with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter: apixaban 5 mg tablet ordered 2026-07-15 (valid 2026-07-15 to 2026-12-23) and rivaroxaban 20 mg tablet ordered two minutes later the same day (valid 2026-07-15 to 2027-01-03). Both cover the evaluation time of 2026-09-24 12:00 and neither has been stopped. Concurrent apixaban and rivaroxaban gives no added benefit and substantially increases bleeding risk (he also has current clopidogrel, prior rectal haemorrhage, thrombocytopenia and anaemia); one agent must be discontinued.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 10:55 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that day contradict this: 107914094 (17:13) and 103088543 (19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 346-718 ms, coefficient of variation 0.16-0.19, RMSSD 98-116 ms) with no discernible P waves - atrial fibrillation at a mean rate of 132-136/min, not sinus rhythm at 72/min. Consistent with the ECGs, unspecified atrial fibrillation was coded at the 2026-06-10 encounter and warfarin was started the same day. The note's rhythm statement is erroneous and should be corrected so the record reflects the diagnosis actually made.

Patient is taking amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication (current order authored 2026-07-12, valid to 2027-01-09). His most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62/min with QT 547 ms at RR 968 ms, i.e. QTc (Bazett) 556 ms - well above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring clinic document of 2025-01-15, so prescriber review is required. QTc was 411 ms on the preceding ECG of 2025-06-07, before amiodarone was started on 2025-11-10. Most recent electrolytes are not contributory: potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (both 2026-06-09). He is also on warfarin, aspirin and clopidogrel; no repeat ECG has been obtained since the QTc prolongation was documented.

This 95-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation/flutter is on continuous amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order authored 2026-06-17, valid to 2027-01-06), a QT watch-list drug. Her most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus bradycardia at 58/min with QT 575 ms at RR 1042 ms, QTc (Bazett) 563 ms, far above the 500 ms review threshold; the prior tracing of 2022-04-06 (atrial fibrillation) had a QTc of 418 ms. Most recent electrolytes are potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (2026-06-17). She is also on warfarin (dose recently reduced for INR 3.4) and metoprolol, which compounds bradycardia-dependent QT risk. No ECG has been recorded since 2022 despite years of amiodarone, so prescriber review and a current ECG are needed.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81/min with smooth respiratory RR variation; upright P in II/III/aVF (P duration ~90 ms) before every QRS, PR 184 ms. Narrow QRS 78 ms, no bundle branch block. QT 329 ms, QTc (Bazett) 381 ms. Frontal QRS axis +47 degrees (normal). No prior ECG in the chart for comparison.

Note the clinic note of 2026-06-10 records 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72' - see the rhythm documentation conflict item.

Regular rhythm at 69/min with a consistent atrial complex preceding every QRS (PR 150 ms); the P vector is leftward/superior (positive in I and aVL, negative in II/III/aVF), so this is a sinus/low-atrial rhythm at normal rate rather than atrial fibrillation. The prior ECG of 2025-04-27 shows inverted P, QRS and T in lead I with positive complexes in aVR and normal precordial leads, i.e. left/right arm lead reversal; allowing for that, the rate, intervals and conduction are unchanged (QTc 404 ms then vs 443 ms now, a 39 ms increase).

Sinus rhythm at 74/min, PR 182 ms (upper normal), QRS 84 ms, QT 381 ms, QTc 423 ms. Axis +53 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart.

Sinus rhythm at 82/min, PR 156 ms, QRS 100 ms (mild non-specific intraventricular conduction delay but not a complete bundle branch block), QT 378 ms, QTc 443 ms. Axis +33 degrees (normal). Only ECG in the chart.

Sinus rhythm at 66/min, PR 156 ms, QRS 88 ms, QT 367 ms, QTc 385 ms. Axis -20 degrees (normal). No bundle branch block. Only ECG in the chart.

Sinus tachycardia at 107/min, regular, PR 162 ms, QRS 66 ms, QT 318 ms, QTc 425 ms, axis +52 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Prior ECG 2019-07-27: sinus rhythm 75/min, PR 154 ms, QRS 68 ms, QTc 427 ms - no change other than the faster rate.

Sinus tachycardia at 121/min, regular. Upright P in II with PR 126 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT 301 ms, QTc 427 ms. Axis +67 degrees (normal). No conduction abnormality. This is the patient's only ECG, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102/min, PR 144 ms, QRS 86 ms, QT 323 ms, QTc 420 ms, axis +58 degrees (normal), no bundle branch block. Atrial fibrillation: irregularly irregular ventricular response (RR 386-1092 ms, coefficient of variation 0.30, RMSSD 265 ms) with no organised P wave anywhere in the TP segments (all atrial deflections <0.05 mV and non-reproducible between beats).
